title: Release the model and retriever as one versioned system
description: Compare a RAFT recipe with the retrieval profile used in production. Each outcome is an illustrative held-out evaluation result, not a forecast.

candidates.label: Balanced RAFT
candidates.detail: 70% oracle-present examples, hard distractors, and explicit evidence targets.

candidates.label: All-oracle RAFT
candidates.detail: Every training context contains answer-bearing evidence; missing-evidence behavior is unpracticed.

candidates.label: Easy-distractor RAFT
candidates.detail: Training negatives are random and lexically distant from the oracle.

retrievers.label: Matched top-5 retriever
retrievers.detail: Same corpus snapshot, chunker, filters, and top-k profile used to create training records.

retrievers.label: New chunker and reranker
retrievers.detail: Longer chunks and a new reranker change oracle position and distractor similarity.

retrievers.label: Broad top-12 retrieval
retrievers.detail: Higher context count improves recall but adds many plausible distractors.

policies.label: Offline experiment
policies.detail: Useful for diagnosis; not an external release.

policies.label: Bounded canary
policies.detail: Limited traffic with monitoring and an immediate rollback path.

policies.label: Production release
policies.detail: The full model-retriever pair must meet the declared evidence contract.

outcomes.note: Training and inference retrieval match; all modeled production gates pass.
The changed retrieval distribution needs new RAFT examples and held-out evaluation.
More retrieved documents raise oracle recall but overwhelm evidence selection.
Evidence use is strong when the oracle appears, but missing-evidence answers are unreliable.
Retriever shift exposes the untrained missing-oracle behavior.
High recall does not compensate for weak distractor and missing-evidence behavior.
The matched retriever still returns harder negatives than the model saw during training.
Both retrieval shift and weak negative training block release.
The larger context exposes the model to many near-neighbor documents it never practiced rejecting.
